title_en: Hershey Drops the Price of Chocolate Bars Back Down to 5 Cents for One Day Only, Here's How to Get One
body_en:
The Hershey movie just opened in theaters, and of course that’s cause for some chocolate festivities. We happen to be in the thick of Black Friday deals , so what better way to celebrate than with a solid discount?
Well, Hershey is taking discounts to a whole new level. For today only, 5oz Hershey chocolate bars have dropped to their retail price from the year 1900: five cents. For reference, in 2026, the chocolate bars typically retail for around $2.
Don’t expect to see the 5-cent Hershey bar everywhere you look - only Amazon, Walmart, and select Hershey store locations are participating in the deal. The Amazon discount went live at 9am EST and will theoretically go away at 9pm EST, unless the retailer decides to offer a little Black Friday treat.
If you’re a real chocoholic, you might as well stock up for the foreseeable future.
Amazon Grocery, which offers same-day delivery, is your best bet for getting the chocolate deal. You can also find the standard Hershey bar discount through Walmart.
Chocolate bars in exclusive vintage packaging are being handed out at two Hershey store locations : the official Hershey location, of course, and the store in Times Square. Hershey notes that the special edition bars available in stores are limited to 10 per person.
The Hershey movie , meanwhile, is now showing in select theaters. It follows Milton Hershey, played by Finn Wittrock, as he builds the chocolate empire we now all know and love.
While the company itself was founded in its initial form in 1897, Hershey didn’t debut the iconic milk chocolate bar until 1900. The bar was launched at the price of a nickel, and its affordability is now considered a major contributing factor to the company’s lasting success. What better way to appreciate the history of the chocolate company than to experience it?
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.
